verses.text: For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm by David. I said, “I'll watch how I act so I don't sin with my words. I'll keep my mouth on a tight leash while the wicked are in front of me.”
I went completely quiet. I held back even good words, and my grief grew.
My heart burned inside me. The more I thought, the hotter it got, until I finally spoke:
“LORD, show me where my life ends and how many days I have. Let me see how fragile I am.
You've made my days only a few handbreadths long. My whole life is like nothing next to you. Even when we stand firm, we're just a breath.” Selah.
“People go around like shadows, rushing for nothing. They pile things up with no idea who'll get them.
So now, Lord, what am I waiting for? My hope is in you.
Rescue me from all my wrongdoing. Don't let fools make me their punch line.
I stayed quiet and didn't open my mouth, because you were the one who did it.
Take this punishment off me. The blow of your hand is more than I can bear.
When you correct people for their sin, you eat away what they treasure like a moth. We're all just a breath.” Selah.
“Hear my prayer, LORD. Listen to my cry. Don't stay silent when I'm in tears. I'm a stranger staying with you, a traveler like all my ancestors.
Please spare me so I can get my strength back before I go away and am gone for good.”
